LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This PKGBUILD appears to be a legitimate AUR package for the Bisq desktop application. The file follows standard Arch Linux packaging practices for a Java/Gradle-based application. The source array contains two git repositories from the official Bisq GitHub organization (the main bisq repo with a signed tag, and bitcoind as a submodule dependency), plus two local support files (desktop entry and launcher). The sha256sums correctly use 'SKIP' for the VCS sources (required practice) and valid checksums for the local files. The validpgpkeys entry is set up for verifying the signed git tag. The prepare() function initializes the bitcoind submodule by pointing it at the locally cloned repo, which is a normal VCS handling pattern. The build() function runs the upstream Gradle build system with appropriate Java settings. The package() functions copy built artifacts to $pkgdir, configure JavaFX module paths via sed (a legitimate need for JavaFX on Linux), and install desktop entries/symlinks. No obfuscated code, dangerous commands (eval, base64, etc.), network data exfiltration, or unexpected system modifications are present. All operations serve the application's stated purpose of providing a decentralized cryptocurrency exchange desktop client.
</details>
